items.explanation: 71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (chart problem list) and no anticoagulant on the current medication list (tamsulosin only; clinic notes 10/2025-7/2026 list no anticoagulant). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis as vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. Only remote hemorrhage complicating a procedure is documented, with no active bleeding contraindication.

Amiodarone (QT watch list) was started at the 11/10/2025 Cardiology Clinic visit, so the 9/1/2025 memo required an ECG within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). A 12-lead ECG was obtained 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met (that tracing shows QTc about 538 ms and is flagged separately for QT review).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at a Cardiology Clinic visit on 3/2/2026, i.e. on or after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo required an ECG within 14 days (by 3/16/2026). A 12-lead ECG was obtained 3/7/2026 (sinus rhythm, QTc about 379 ms), 5 days after the start, meeting the requirement.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at a Cardiology Clinic visit on 2/12/2026; because the start was before 3/1/2026 the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (due 3/14/2026). A 12-lead ECG was obtained 3/8/2026 (sinus rhythm, QTc about 450 ms), 24 days after the start, meeting the requirement.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at a Cardiology Clinic visit on 4/10/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days (by 4/24/2026). The only ECG in the chart was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not met in time and is overdue as of 9/24/2026 (that tracing showed sinus rhythm with QTc about 388 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at a Cardiology Clinic visit on 8/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days (by 8/15/2026). No ECG has been recorded since the start (the only tracing in the chart is from 12/25/2025), so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at a Cardiology Clinic visit on 8/10/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days (by 8/24/2026). No ECG is in the chart, but the 8/25/2026 nurse telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 (within the window) and the report was requested but not yet received, so completion cannot be determined until that report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 9/15/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start, but the window has not yet closed as of the 9/24/2026 review, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the 9/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit Dr. Kessler increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily for a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6, so the 3/1/2026 memo required an INR within 7 days (by 9/8/2026). INR 2.3 was drawn 9/5/2026, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

On 9/10/2026 the clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the anticoagulation protocol after a home INR of 3.4, so a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days (by 9/17/2026). No INR has been resulted since 8/22/2026 (INR 2.6), so the follow-up INR is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes from 9/12/2025 through 5/28/2026 all document persistent atrial fibrillation, yet the current medication list is only aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg (active orders 5/28/2026 to 1/2027) - no oral anticoagulant. CHA2DS2-VASc is 9 (age >=75 2, prior cerebral infarction/TIA 2, heart failure 1, hypertension 1, diabetes 1, coronary/old MI vascular disease 1, female 1). Guideline-directed anticoagulation is strongly recommended and aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis; no bleeding contraindication is documented.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on the problem list and prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia. Current medications (clinic notes through 7/10/2026 and active orders) are carvedilol, metoprolol and famotidine only - no anticoagulant. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (prior stroke 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1); guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. No documented absolute contraindication (thrombocytopenia and falls noted historically) - needs prescriber review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 8/20/2026 (valid through 12/28/2026) although the 8/12/2026 outside-records summary documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (hemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel add further bleeding risk. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but both prescriptions were issued that day and both are still current on 9/24/2026: apixaban 5 mg BID (valid to 12/26/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (valid to 12/25/2026). Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding hazard; one must be discontinued.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that day (17:13 and 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response at 139-144 bpm with no discernible P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rates. The documented rhythm and rate conflict with the same-day tracings and the chart should be corrected/reviewed (the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin, and rate control may be needed).

Most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm 68 bpm with QT about 490 ms and Bazett QTc about 520 ms, above the 500 ms clinic threshold, while escitalopram 10 mg daily remains a current order (re-issued 4/23/2026, valid to 1/2/2027). Most recent electrolytes (8/23/2025) are normal: K 4.1 mEq/L, Mg 2.1 mg/dL. The 5/14/2024 note called the QT acceptable, but the tracing meets the clinic review threshold; prescriber review of the QT-prolonging drug and a repeat ECG are needed.

Most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm 62 bpm with QT about 530 ms and Bazett QTc about 538 ms (>=500 ms) while amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (re-issued 7/29/2026, valid to 1/5/2027). Most recent electrolytes (4/20/2026) normal: K 4.4 mEq/L, Mg 2.2 mg/dL. QTc rose from 438 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing after amiodarone was started; prescriber review required.

Most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm 70 bpm with QT about 505 ms and Bazett QTc about 546 ms (>=500 ms) while citalopram 40 mg daily is a current order (re-issued 5/29/2026, valid to 12/25/2026); 40 mg exceeds the 20 mg maximum usually advised when QT is prolonged. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (1/21/2026); most recent magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (12/1/2023). Prescriber review of dose and repeat ECG needed.

Most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm 57 bpm with QT about 555 ms and Bazett QTc about 540 ms (>=500 ms) while amiodarone 200 mg daily remains a current order (re-issued 8/22/2026, valid to 1/5/2027). Most recent electrolytes (2/14/2026): K 4.1 mEq/L, Mg 1.8 mg/dL (low-normal). QTc increased from 430 ms on the 4/6/2022 tracing; prescriber review and an updated ECG are needed.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with an upright P wave before every QRS in lead II (PR 178 ms). QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +45 (normal), rS in V1 with a dominant R in V5-V6 and no bundle branch block. QT about 327 ms, Bazett QTc about 379 ms - well below the 500 ms threshold despite citalopram therapy. No earlier tracing is available for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, regular, with upright P waves in lead II (PR about 130 ms). QRS 100 ms, axis about +40 (normal), deep S in V1 without bundle branch block. QT about 365 ms, QTc about 480 ms (mildly prolonged). The prior tracing (6/20/2025) showed a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 147 bpm with 1:1 P waves (sinus tachycardia) and QTc in the low 400s; rhythm unchanged and the QTc difference does not clearly reach 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with P waves before each QRS (PR about 115 ms), QRS 90 ms, axis about +37 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 340 ms with QTc about 460 ms (borderline prolonged, below the 500 ms threshold). No prior ECG for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: RR intervals vary from 348 to 648 ms (CV 0.16) with no organised P waves, so no PR interval is measurable; mean rate about 144 bpm. QRS 84 ms, axis about +5 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 280 ms, QTc about 432 ms. The tracing recorded 2 hours earlier the same day also showed AF at about 139 bpm with QTc about 435 ms, so there is no change; note the same-day clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' conflicts with both tracings.

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with consistent P waves and PR about 130 ms; a single late premature beat accounts for the RR variability. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about -25 (normal, leftward), no bundle branch block. QT about 410 ms, QTc about 441 ms. Prior tracing (4/27/2025) showed sinus rhythm at 60 bpm with QTc about 406 ms and markedly different limb-lead polarity (probable lead reversal); no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular, with upright P waves in lead II (PR about 100 ms). QRS 72 ms, axis about +5 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 305 ms, QTc about 388 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular, with low-amplitude but consistent P waves (PR about 135 ms). QRS 90 ms, axis about +20 (normal), rS in V1 without bundle branch block. QT about 375 ms, QTc about 415 ms - below the 500 ms threshold, although this tracing predates the escitalopram started 8/1/2026. No prior ECG for comparison.

Atrial fibrillation: RR intervals range from 470 to 1148 ms (CV 0.27) with no organised atrial activity, so no PR interval is measurable; mean ventricular rate about 82 bpm. QRS 98 ms, axis about +27 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 435 ms, QTc about 510 ms. The tracing three days earlier (11/12/2024) showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves and QTc about 407 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation with a QTc increase of more than 60 ms. The patient is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with upright P waves (PR about 105 ms), QRS 90 ms, axis about +60 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 400 ms, QTc about 396 ms. Prior tracing the previous day showed sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QTc about 438 ms; no change of 60 ms or more. This tracing predates the haloperidol started 9/15/2026.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, very regular, with P waves before each QRS (PR about 140 ms). QRS 76 ms, axis about +52 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 345 ms, QTc about 406 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with P waves before each QRS (PR about 145 ms), QRS 72 ms, axis about +65 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 405 ms, QTc about 459 ms. The prior tracing (2/2/2020) showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with a low-amplitude inverted T wave and QTc about 530 ms, so the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms; rhythm unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm with regular RR intervals (CV 0.01) and a P wave preceding each QRS; PR about 110 ms, QRS 84 ms, axis about +50 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 275 ms with QTc about 387 ms. Compared with the 9/16/2016 tracing (sinus 108 bpm, QTc about 390 ms) the rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm. Each QRS is preceded by a P wave but the PR interval is prolonged at about 210 ms, consistent with first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms, axis about 0 (normal); tall R in V1-V2 and prominent R in V5-V6 without a bundle branch block pattern. QT about 400 ms, QTc about 381 ms. Prior tracing (11/30/2024) showed sinus rhythm at 51 bpm with PR about 185 ms and QTc about 364 ms; no flagged change (QTc difference under 60 ms).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: RR intervals vary from 302 to 580 ms with no consistent P waves, so no PR interval is measurable; mean rate about 154 bpm. QRS narrow (about 65 ms), axis about -10 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 260 ms, QTc about 412 ms. The prior tracing (9/12/2025) also showed atrial fibrillation (mean rate about 77 bpm, QTc about 415 ms), so there is no rhythm or QTc change. The patient is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with upright P waves and PR about 165 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis about +10 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 355 ms, QTc about 393 ms, matching the same-day clinic note of sinus rhythm. The prior tracing (11/21/2025) showed sinus rhythm with frequent atrial premature beats and a much longer QT (QTc about 537 ms), so the QTc has decreased by more than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with P waves before each QRS (PR about 180 ms) and mild respiratory RR variation. QRS 88 ms, axis about +53 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 365 ms, QTc about 408 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, regular, with large P waves in lead II (PR about 165 ms). QRS 86 ms, axis about +34 (normal); very deep S in V1 with tall lateral R waves (voltage criteria for LVH) but no bundle branch block. QT about 300 ms, QTc about 408 ms. Prior tracing (7/4/2022) showed the same sinus tachycardia at 115 bpm with QTc about 383 ms; no change flags.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm: P waves of constant morphology precede each QRS with PR about 195 ms, and the RR variability is due to one premature beat followed by a compensatory pause (no fibrillatory baseline). QRS 102 ms, frontal axis about -31 (left axis deviation), no bundle branch block. QT about 370 ms, QTc about 375 ms. This single tracing does not capture the documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and no prior ECG is available.

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular, with atrial activity before each QRS (PR about 135 ms). QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block. Net QRS is strongly negative in lead I and slightly negative in aVF, giving an extreme (northwest) frontal axis of about -173; low limb-lead voltage and possible lead misplacement should be considered. QT about 360 ms, QTc about 388 ms - no QT prolongation on escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with upright P waves (PR about 155 ms), QRS 92 ms, axis about +36 (normal), no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad and late with QT about 505 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms - markedly prolonged on citalopram 40 mg daily. The prior tracing (6/17/2020) showed sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc about 435 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with P waves before each QRS (PR about 135 ms), QRS 86 ms, axis about +60 (normal), no bundle branch block. The T wave is prominent in the limb leads and returns to baseline by about 425 ms, giving QT about 425 ms and QTc about 453 ms - prolonged but below the 500 ms threshold for a patient on escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison; this tracing satisfied the post-start monitoring requirement.

Technically poor, very low-voltage tracing (all leads under 0.15 mV). Underlying rhythm is sinus at about 61 bpm with P waves before most beats (PR about 190 ms) and several atrial premature beats producing the RR irregularity. QRS appears narrow (about 70 ms) and is too small for reliable morphology assessment; no bundle branch block pattern is evident. Measured frontal axis is leftward (about -75) but unreliable at this voltage. QT about 350 ms, QTc about 352 ms. Prior tracing (12/13/2018) showed sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, PR about 200 ms, QRS 108 ms and QTc about 390 ms; no change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR about 130 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis about +40 (normal), no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad and flat with QT about 490 ms and Bazett QTc about 520 ms - markedly prolonged and above the clinic threshold for a patient on escitalopram. The prior tracing (11/23/2022) had QTc about 354 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms; the rhythm is unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm: RR intervals are regular (402-454 ms, CV 0.02) and each QRS is preceded by a P wave (PR about 115 ms). QRS 76 ms, axis about 0 (normal), no bundle branch block or pacing spikes. QT about 270 ms, QTc about 413 ms. The prior tracing (7/11/2022) showed atrial fibrillation with an irregular response at about 111 bpm (QTc about 429 ms), so atrial fibrillation has resolved; QTc unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular, with P waves before each QRS (PR about 135 ms). QRS 104 ms - mildly widened but below 120 ms, so no bundle branch block. Axis about +34 (normal). QT about 380 ms, QTc about 447 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular, with P waves before each QRS (PR about 185 ms). QRS 74 ms, axis about -16 (normal, leftward), no bundle branch block. QT about 335 ms, QTc about 412 ms. Prior tracing (5/16/2021) showed sinus rhythm at 87 bpm with QTc about 397 ms; no change flags.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with a P wave before each QRS but a prolonged PR of about 210 ms (first-degree AV block). QRS is wide at about 134 ms with a QS/deep S pattern in V1-V2 and a broad monophasic R in I, aVL and V6 - complete left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -21 (within the normal range). QT about 450 ms, QTc about 458 ms (interpret with caution in the presence of LBBB). The prior tracing (6/3/2024) showed the same sinus rhythm with LBBB (QRS 134 ms) and QTc about 454 ms, so there is no new conduction abnormality or QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, regular, with prominent P waves (PR about 145 ms). QRS 80 ms, axis about +45 (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 320 ms, QTc about 415 ms. Prior tracing the previous day showed sinus rhythm at 102 bpm with QTc about 412 ms; unchanged.

Low-voltage tracing showing sinus rhythm at about 73 bpm: P waves of consistent amplitude precede the sinus beats (PR about 155 ms) and the RR irregularity is explained by several atrial premature beats, including a couplet, rather than fibrillation. QRS 80 ms, axis about -22 (normal, leftward), no bundle branch block. QT about 365 ms, QTc about 402 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 57 bpm with organised P waves before each QRS (PR about 195 ms), QRS 88 ms, axis about +37 (normal), no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad and late: QT about 555 ms with Bazett QTc about 540 ms - markedly prolonged on amiodarone. The prior tracing (4/6/2022) showed atrial fibrillation at about 129 bpm with QTc about 430 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm, regular, with P waves before each QRS (PR about 160 ms). QRS 68 ms, axis about +51 (normal), no bundle branch block. The T wave ends about 340 ms after QRS onset (the following deflection is the next P wave), giving QT about 340 ms and QTc about 460 ms. Prior tracing (7/27/2019) showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with QTc about 432 ms; the difference is less than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, perfectly regular, with a discrete P wave before each QRS (PR about 125 ms). QRS 80 ms, axis about +70 (normal), no conduction block. QT about 290 ms, QTc about 408 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101 bpm with 1:1 P waves (PR about 140 ms), QRS 86 ms, axis about +58 (normal), deep S in V1 with tall R in V5-V6 but no bundle branch block. QT about 320 ms, QTc about 414 ms. Essentially identical to the tracing recorded 34 minutes earlier (sinus 100 bpm, QTc about 406 ms); no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with a P wave before every QRS (PR about 170 ms) - no dropped beats on this tracing despite the history of Mobitz II block. QRS 92 ms, axis about +36 (normal); tall R in V5-V6 (voltage criteria for LVH) without bundle branch block. QT about 435 ms, QTc about 405 ms. Prior tracing (5/22/2023) showed sinus rhythm at 57 bpm with a single pause and QTc about 361 ms; no change flags (QTc difference under 60 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular, with a small P wave before each QRS (PR about 120 ms). QRS 84 ms with an rSr' in V1 that does not reach 120 ms, so the tracing does not meet criteria for complete right bundle branch block. Net QRS is negative in leads I and aVL with a positive III and aVR, giving a rightward frontal axis of about +140 (right axis deviation, low limb-lead voltage - consider lead placement). QT about 290 ms, QTc about 416 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (01:33) showed a regular rhythm at 100 bpm with similar rSR' in V1 and QTc in the same range; no change flags.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with organised P waves and constant PR (about 170 ms) for the first nine beats and a single late premature beat. QRS 100 ms, axis about +65 (normal), no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad with QT about 530 ms and Bazett QTc about 538 ms - markedly prolonged on amiodarone. The prior tracing (6/7/2025) showed atrial fibrillation with an irregular ventricular response and QTc about 438 ms, so sinus rhythm has been restored (AF resolved) but the QTc has increased by about 100 ms.

Atrial fibrillation: RR intervals are irregularly irregular (408-730 ms, CV 0.19) with no discernible P waves, so no PR interval can be measured. Mean ventricular rate about 107 bpm. QRS 82 ms with a leftward frontal axis of about -48 (left axis deviation) and no bundle branch block. QT about 320 ms, QTc about 425 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible; the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.
